messages.subject: Attention: bug in read.genalex --- strata mis-aligned with entirely non-typed individuals
messages.subject_clean: Attention: bug in read.genalex --- strata mis-aligned with entirely non-typed individuals
messages.body_plain:
Brought up by Hernán Dario Capador-Barreto, there is a bug where the strata is not properly subset when non-typed individuals (those with all missing data) are removed, resulting in incorrect strata assignments from read.genalex with these type of data (see https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues/147 for reference).

This will be fixed in the upcoming poppr version 2.5.0 (I will be sending an email announcement for the pre-release shortly). In the meantime, the fix for this issue is to re-assign the strata from the population before splitting it (example below).

library("poppr")
#> Loading required package: adegenet
#> Loading required package: ade4
#>
#>    /// adegenet 2.1.0 is loaded ////////////
#>
#>    > overview: '?adegenet'
#>    > tutorials/doc/questions: 'adegenetWeb()'
#>    > bug reports/feature requests: adegenetIssues()
#> This is poppr version 2.5.0. To get started, type package?poppr
#> OMP parallel support: available
missing_single <- "13\t6\t1\t6
7_09_BB
Ind\tPop\tCHMFc4\tCHMFc5\tCHMFc12\tSEA\tSED\tSEE\tSEG\tSEI\tSEL\tSEN\tSEP\tSEQ\tSER
A004\t7_09_BB_A004\t224\t85\t163\t132\t133\t156\t144\t116\t143\t227\t257\t142\t145
A002\t7_09_BB_A002\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0
A011\t7_09_BB_A011\t224\t97\t159\t160\t133\t156\t126\t119\t147\t227\t257\t134\t149
A009\t7_09_BB_A009\t224\t97\t159\t160\t133\t156\t126\t119\t147\t227\t261\t134\t149
A006\t7_09_BB_A006\t224\t97\t159\t160\t133\t156\t126\t119\t147\t235\t261\t134\t149
A013\t7_09_BB_A013\t224\t97\t163\t160\t133\t156\t126\t119\t147\t235\t257\t134\t149"
dat <- read.genalex(textConnection(missing_single), sep = "\t")
#> Warning in df2genind(gena, ind.names = ind.vec, pop = pop.vec, ploidy =
#> 1, : entirely non-type individual(s) deleted
strata(dat)  # incorrect
#>               Pop
#> A004 7_09_BB_A004
#> A011 7_09_BB_A002
#> A009 7_09_BB_A011
#> A006 7_09_BB_A009
#> A013 7_09_BB_A006
data.frame(pop(dat))  # correct
#>       pop.dat.
#> 1 7_09_BB_A004
#> 2 7_09_BB_A011
#> 3 7_09_BB_A009
#> 4 7_09_BB_A006
#> 5 7_09_BB_A013

# Temporary solution: reset the strata
strata(dat) <- data.frame(Pop = pop(dat))
strata(dat)
#>            Pop
#> 1 7_09_BB_A004
#> 2 7_09_BB_A011
#> 3 7_09_BB_A009
#> 4 7_09_BB_A006
#> 5 7_09_BB_A013

Best,
Zhian

messages.subject: Poppr version 2.5.0 pre-release
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am pleased to announce the pre-release version of poppr 2.5.0. Details are available at https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/releases/tag/v.2.5.0rcv1

It contains a major bug fix for those who deal with polyploid data and Bruvo's distance with either genome addition or genome loss corrections. It also contains a bug fix for read.genalex. We have ensured that all the new functionality is tested accurately, but nevertheless, if you run into any major bugs or otherwise unexpected results, please open an issue at https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues.

I plan to submit the new version to CRAN by next week. If you wish to test out this version before it hits CRAN, and have OSX or Windows, you can install it like so (otherwise, use devtools):

# For OSX users
install.packages("https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/releases/download/v.2.5.0rcv1/poppr_2.5.0rcv1.tgz", repos = NULL)

# For Windows users
install.packages("https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/releases/download/v.2.5.0rcv1/poppr_2.5.0rcv1.zip", repos = NULL)

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.subject: Poppr version 2.5.0 is released on CRAN
messages.subject_clean: Poppr version 2.5.0 is released on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Poppr version 2.5.0 has been released.

The binary for Windows users will be on CRAN within the next 24 hours.

Copy and Paste this code into your R console:

install.packages("poppr", repos = "https://cran.rstudio.com")

Below you can find details of this release and other poppr-related news.

Details
----------

This release is mainly for compatibility with dplyr 0.7 and bug fixes, but the bug fixes were significant enough to warrant more than just a patch release.

Main points:

 - Fixed a bug in read.genalex() where entirely missing samples would accidentally shift the strata (details: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues/147)
 - For those who deal with polyploid data that have more than ambiguous alleles, Bruvo's distance will now consider all ordered combinations of alleles with the genome addition and loss models (details: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues/139)

A full list of changes can be found here: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/releases/tag/v.2.5.0

Poppr reference website
------------------------------------

I have launched a website for browsing the reference manual at https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/

It contains examples that have been rendered so you can compare the output with what is expected. For example, here's the example for bruvo.dist: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/bruvo.dist.html#examples

Cheers!
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] How to m aboot tree more clear and separated tree for better understanding?
messages.subject_clean: [poppr] How to m aboot tree more clear and separated tree for better understanding?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

With the output you get, you can plot the tree using the plot.phylo function in ape (https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/ape/versions/4.1/topics/plot.phylo)

There are a lot of parameters, so you will need to play around with them to get an optimal solution. Otherwise, you may need to increase your canvas size: https://stackoverflow.com/a/7405548/2752888

There is also the ggtree package on Bioconductor: https://guangchuangyu.github.io/ggtree/

Sorry I'm not able to give you one perfect solution. I hope these can help get you started.

Zhian

-----
Zhian N. Kamvar, Ph. D.
Postdoctoral Researcher (Everhart Lab)
Department of Plant Pathology
University of Nebraska-Lincoln
